answers.children: Weimaraners are moderately good with children. Their large size and high energy mean they can knock over toddlers during enthusiastic games of fetch while their loyal and intelligent nature helps them bond with older kids who join outdoor activities; the breed was developed to work closely with humans in the field which supports their affectionate leaning but demands supervision around small children due to rambunctious play. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Weimaraners can get along with other pets when raised together. Their hunting background for large game gives them a prey drive that makes them chase smaller animals while their loyal temperament reduces same-sex tension with familiar dogs if properly socialised though wariness of strangers extends to unfamiliar pets.
answers.exercise: Weimaraners need one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise. Runs hikes or intense fetch sessions suit their exceptional stamina for outdoor activities and hunting heritage while insufficient activity leads to destructive behaviour such as shredded couch cushions or dug-up gardens because their boundless energy and intelligence cause boredom without outlets.
answers.shedding: Yes — Weimaraners shed moderately with short single coats that release silver-gray hair year-round onto furniture and clothing. The sleek texture means loose hairs cling noticeably to fabrics yet the minimal length avoids heavy matting so regular brushing controls the spread from their energetic movement indoors after hunts.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic yet Weimaraners are not among those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Their short single coat still produces dander and releases moderate amounts of silver-gray hair that spreads through the home especially after vigorous activity so the sleek build offers no relief for sensitive owners.
answers.training: Weimaraners are easy to train. Their high intelligence and trainability for hunting and sports allow quick learning of commands and routines yet their energetic stubborn streak can lead to boundary testing if owners lack consistency matching the breed's history of close human partnership in rugged terrain.
answers.lifespan: Weimaraners live 10-13 years. Their large athletic build from German hunting lines supports active years but the profile notes only average health robustness so endurance for all-day hunts does not guarantee extended longevity without proper management of their high-energy demands.
answers.size: Weimaraners reach 55-90 lb and stand 23-27 in tall. The sleek muscular build feels substantial when a loyal 70-pound adult leans for affection or races through the house creating a noticeable presence that suits their history as versatile hunters capable of tracking large game across rugged ground.
answers.barking: Weimaraners bark moderately. Bred in Germany to hunt large game like deer and boar they stay relatively quiet during focused work but their intelligent and loyal nature leads to vocalising when bored or anxious from separation which can increase if their high energy lacks sufficient daily outlets for stamina.
answers.apartment: Weimaraners do not suit apartment living. Their high energy and need for one to two hours of vigorous exercise daily combined with potential destructive behaviour from boredom make settling indoors difficult while their loyal attachment often produces anxious vocalisations that disturb neighbours despite the breed's trainable intelligence.
answers.first-time: Weimaraners are not a good first dog. Their high energy that leads to destructive behaviour without exercise and tendency toward separation anxiety demand experienced owners who can provide consistent training and activity matching the breed's intelligent loyal temperament developed for all-day hunting partnership.
